newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Foxtel first half net loss A$98 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Foxtel first half net loss A$98 mln.

text.p: Australian pay television operator Foxtel, jointly owned by News Corp Ltd and Telstra Corp, reported a loss of A$98 million for the six months ended December 31, 1996.
Foxtel said it currently has over 150,000 active subscribers. It said cable ready homes marketed by Foxtel grew to 900,000 from 700,000 during the period.
Foxtel, which started operations in late 1995, reported a loss of A$165 million for the year to June 30, 1996.
All three of Australia's pay television companies recorded big losses in the 1996/97 first half.
Cable TV operator Optus Vision reported a loss of A$168 million for the December 1996 half and satellite pay TV operator Australis Media Ltd reported a loss of A$141 million in the first half.
Australia's pay television industry has recorded losses of over A$1.0 billion in its brief history. The losses mainly reflect the cost of start-up of the operations.
